summary: Consolidate CI service identities and remove broad cloud-owner bindings across AWS & GCP test accounts
description:
Issue summary: Security audit discovered multiple CI service principals with overly broad roles (OrganizationOwner / Owner) in both AWS test accounts and GCP project sandboxes. This ticket is to consolidate those identities into a small, auditable set of service accounts with least-privilege roles and to remove any direct Owner/OrgOwner bindings from CI runner identities.

Impact: Potential for accidental or malicious privilege escalation from compromised CI runners; increases blast radius for config drift and deployment automation. No active exploit identified, but policy requires remediation before next quarterly audit.

Background: During the Feb 2026 internal IAM sweep (security-runbook v3), we flagged ~7 CI runner identities across two AWS accounts and three GCP projects that have owner-level permissions. These identities were created at different times by multiple teams and are referenced in a mix of GitHub Actions, CircleCI, and an internal self-hosted Runner Fleet. Ad-hoc fixes have been applied previously, but we need a coordinated consolidation and role-replacement plan that preserves CI workflows and secrets access.

Request: 1) Inventory every CI-related service principal/service account across the listed environments and map usages (pipelines, vault policies, KMS keys). 2) Create 2 standardized service accounts per cloud (ci-build, ci-deploy) with narrowly scoped roles and condition-based bindings. 3) Implement IAM bindings via IaC (Terraform modules) and revoke legacy Owner/OrgOwner bindings. 4) Update runbooks and rotate short-lived credentials/keys as part of cutover.

Constraints/Non-goals: This ticket does not include rearchitecting CI tooling (e.g., replacing CircleCI). We will avoid changes that require immediate changes to customer-facing deployments. Migration windows must be schedulable with team owners.

Acceptance criteria: - Inventory documented in linked Confluence page. - Terraform modules reviewed in a GitHub PR and merged. - No CI runner identity has Owner/OrgOwner after cutover. - CI pipelines validated in staging and smoke-tested in prod. - Post-change IAM scan shows reduction in owner-level principals by >=90%.
steps_to_reproduce: Run internal iam-scan v2 against AWS account: aws-test-1 and aws-test-2 (script: tools/iam_scan.sh) to list principals with AdministratorAccess or Owner policies.
Run gcloud asset search-all-iam-policies for projects: ci-sandbox-eu, ci-sandbox-us, ci-staging to surface serviceAccount bindings to roles/owner.
Correlate principals to CI pipeline config (repo .github/workflows, .circleci/config.yml) to find usages.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-02: Initial audit produced CSV of principals; 7 candidates identified (4 AWS IAM roles, 3 GCP service accounts).
2026-03-03: Confirmed two AWS roles are referenced by legacy CircleCI runners; owners are @infra-legacy and @data-eng.
2026-03-04: One GCP service account is used for KMS unwrap in a deploy pipeline; will require a key-binding migration or a short-lived key approach.

Hypothesis: Historical convenience overrides (Owner role) were used for speed. Least-privilege roles can be implemented by scoping to specific APIs (kms.cryptoKeyVersions.useToDecrypt, storage.objects.get) and resource-level RBAC.
Risk note: Removing Owner from the deploy identity without staging cutover will break scheduled releases; schedule a canary deploy window.

resolution_notes: In progress: terraform module 'ci-service-accounts' created in infra-iam repo (PR referenced). Staged bindings applied to staging account on 2026-03-11; successful pipeline runs observed. Legacy Owner bindings scheduled to be revoked in a maintenance window 2026-03-15.
Follow-up: create automation to detect owner-level bindings weekly and alert #infra-iam with a one-click remediation runbook.
